hero.eyebrow: AI crop assistant for maize farmers
hero.lede: Take a photo of a maize leaf. We identify Maize Lethal Necrosis, Maize Streak Virus or Northern Leaf Blight, show how severe it is, and tell you exactly what to do next.

healthy.label: Healthy
healthy.meaning: No signs of disease. This leaf looks like a healthy maize leaf.
steps: Keep checking a few plants across the field every week.
Keep grass weeds down. They shelter the insects that spread maize viruses.

mild.label: Mild
mild.meaning: Early stage: only small parts of the leaf are affected.
steps: Mark this plant and check it again in 3 to 5 days.
Check the plants around it for the same signs.
Follow the disease steps below to stop it spreading.

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.meaning: A clear part of this leaf is damaged.
steps: Follow the disease steps below today.
Ask an extension officer to confirm before buying any product.
Check the neighbouring plants for the same signs.

severe.label: Severe
severe.meaning: Most of this leaf is damaged. The plant can spread disease to the rest of the field.
steps: Pull out the plant and destroy it away from the field (bury or burn it).
Do not leave diseased plants or leaves lying in the field.
Wash your hands and tools afterwards.
Tell your extension officer, especially if many plants look like this.

MLND.name: Maize Lethal Necrosis
MLND.kind: Virus · spread by thrips, aphids and seed
MLND.signs: Fine yellow specks and stripes from the base of young leaves that join into mottled patches, then dry out from the leaf edges. The youngest leaves can die ("dead heart") and cobs stay small.
MLND.cause: Two viruses together, carried by thrips and aphids, and by contaminated seed, tools and crop residue.
steps: Scout often and pull out infected plants straight away.
Plant certified seed of MLN-tolerant hybrids.
Keep grass weeds down, and don't intercrop maize with cabbage, kale or onions.
Seed dressed with a systemic insecticide protects young plants. Ask an agro-dealer.
Leave the field without maize for at least 2 months, and rotate with beans or other legumes.
Clean tools after working in an infected field.

MSV.name: Maize Streak Virus
MSV.signs: Narrow, unbroken pale-yellow streaks along the leaf veins, starting on the youngest leaves. Plants infected young stay stunted.
MSV.cause: A virus carried by small leafhoppers. It does not spread through seed.
steps: Plant a streak-resistant variety. Ask your agro-dealer which ones resist streak in your area.
Plant early in the season, at the same time as your neighbours.
Pull out infected young plants early.
Keep grass weeds down around the field.
MSV.risk: Losses of up to 90% on susceptible varieties.

MLB.name: Northern Leaf Blight
MLB.kind: Fungus · spread by wind and rain
MLB.signs: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan spots, starting on the lower leaves and moving up the plant. Worse in cool, wet weather.
MLB.cause: A fungus that survives on old maize residue in the field.
steps: Plant a tolerant or resistant hybrid. This is the most reliable control.
Rotate maize with another crop.
Remove or bury maize residue after harvest.
Use a fungicide only if an extension officer recommends one.
MLB.risk: Losses of up to 60% in Kenya.

about.title: How MaizeCare works
about.model_body: The first model recognises the disease. The second learned what healthy maize leaves look like and measures how far your leaf is from healthy.
about.privacy_body: Photos are analysed in memory and deleted straight away. Nothing is stored and no account is needed.
about.advice_body: Based on East African crop research and under review with an agricultural extension officer.

footer.disclaimer: Not a substitute for advice from your local extension officer.
